$comment: Machine-readable contract for everything this project assumes about
jav8.vip, and for the download-client defaults.
The userscript has to ship as a single file, so these values are inlined
in the script. test/parity.test.mjs asserts the inlined copies match this
file, so they cannot drift apart silently.
Every claim below is measured against captured pages or a stock client
install, and the note beside it says which - see README.md for the method.

notes: The site injects promotional cards with absolute hrefs via its adworker
script. Requiring the /v/ prefix on the card selector skips them.
Studio-strip cards have no cover image and get no tick box.
Pagination is a plain ?page=N query on every paginated route, and every
one of them renders the same control: <a class="pagination-next"
href="...">. The last page omits it, which is the only reliable end
signal - there is no total count in the markup to compute the page
count from. Verified on /actress/<id> (a 7-page career paginates to

selectors.$comment: CSS selectors verified against captured pages in test/fixtures.

$comment: 1024-based on purpose: the site labels GiB as GB almost everywhere, and
one consistent basis keeps every window comparison self-consistent.
The rule is: title marker OR a VR substring in the code prefix.
Measured disagreement between the two signals is the reason both are
needed: the title marker caught 17/17 known VR releases, the code
pattern caught 6 more that the title missed, and the code pattern
produced zero false positives across 98 flat releases.
A hand-listed set of prefixes was tried first and caught only 6 of 26,
so it is deliberately not used.
Do not treat 第一人称 (first person) as a VR signal: it appears on many
ordinary flat releases.
A meaningful share of magnet entries are adverts. Across 262 real
entries the three tiers below separate them cleanly: no clean release
matched an ad rule, and no advert escaped one.
The bare @ is deliberate. An earlier rule required a domain after it
and so missed real entries such as 第一會所新片@SIS001@DDH-451 and
ALDN-433.[4K]@R90s, where nothing follows the @ but a dotted domain.

ad.wordsPattern: (夸克|無广告|无广告|旗舰APP|成人APP|1视频|月新地址)

suspect.note: Deprioritised, used only when no clean release exists.

clean.note: A plain catalog name such as IPZZ-961 or 259LUXU-1900.

$comment: Release tags read from the magnet filename, and the preferences built on
them. See magnetTags() and applyTagPrefs() in the userscript.
Measured, not guessed: 783 magnets across 80 work pages, drawn from twelve
performers' filmographies after a first sample from /updated and /latest
turned out to contain none of these flags at all - 0 of 149. Which studios
a sample happens to hit matters more than how many pages it covers.
Each fact has two near-disjoint spellings and only one of them is commonly
used: -U and 无码 co-occur on 5 of 736 releases, and -C and 中文字幕 on none
of them. They are alternative conventions from different uploaders, so
matching one spelling matches about half of what it claims to cover.
-CN does not occur on this site (0 of 783) and is deliberately not a rule.
無修正 likewise does not occur, but is accepted anyway as the
traditional-script spelling of the same words as 无码.
Only 14% of releases carry any tag. A requirement that cannot be met
therefore relaxes rather than blocking, and that is the common case, not
an edge case - see applyTagPrefs().

sample.source: actress filmographies; /updated and /latest carry none of these flags

uncensored.note: -UC is also chinese; it is the intersection of the two categories.

uhd.note: Also matched without a catalogue code, e.g. ipzz703.4K.mp4.

magnetTags.precedence: explicit requirements narrow first; the AI veto relaxes last

worthIt.note: Why the preferences exist: they choose between magnets of the SAME work.

$comment: The site injects its own advert cards into every listing. They are built at
runtime by an inline adworker() script, so no captured fixture has ever
contained one - tools/fetch_fixtures.py strips that script on purpose.
Measured from the live page rather than from a fixture; see adworker().
An advert is a real-looking work card that links OFF this site. That is the
rule, and it is close to definitional: the point of an advert is to send
you somewhere else. It is compared against the page's own host, so an
advert from a domain nobody has seen yet is still caught.
The previous rule looked for promo wording in the card's title and could
never have fired, for two reasons that are both facts about this markup:
the cards are linked with an absolute href, so the /v/ card selector never
matched them; and they have no .work-title element at all.
These are not works, so they are hidden outside the VR filter and counted
separately from it. They cannot be selected: they carry no /v/ href, so
they are absent from worksOnPage() and therefore from select-all, from the
selection and from a + crawl.
Costs no requests - it reads the href the markup already has.
adCards.injector: inline adworker(), prmt() template, two cards per listing
adCards.markup:
91Porn

promo

$comment: How a listing card is matched against a file in the user's own media
library. See codeKey(), codeKeys() and libraryIndexOf() in the userscript.
The join is the catalogue number, not the title: a card carries

fex-004

and a work page carries the same
value in <dt class="highlight">ipzz-961</dt>, so the site's end is exact
at both places. The library's end is not - it is whatever the file was
called - so codes are extracted from free text there rather than compared.
The key is the alphanumerics with separators removed and leading zeros
dropped from the trailing digit run. Both transformations are needed by
real filenames: fex-004, fex004, FEX 004 and h_259fex00004 are the same
work, and so are DDH-0045 and DDH-45.
A numeric prefix is kept when the whole thing is the code (259LUXU-1900 is
a real series), and dropped as an extra key when it is a maker prefix
(DMM writes h_<maker><code><padded number>). Both keys are emitted for a
match with a leading digit run rather than guessing which shape a filename
means, because the two conventions look identical.
The extractor requires two letters and two digits, which is the entire
noise rule: x264, AV1, CD1, MP4 and 1080p all fail it, while HD1080 passes
and is harmless because a real catalogue code is never HD-1080.
codeMatching.keyRule: uppercase alphanumerics, separators removed, leading zeros dropped from the trailing digit run

verifiedOnRealLibrary.note: Checked against a real Jellyfin rather than only invented filenames. Of 34 catalogue codes taken from the captured listing fixture, 5 were genuinely held and every one matched the right work; the other 29 matched nothing. No key that the site can produce was claimed by more than one file, and every one of the 1869 code-like paths resolved to itself.
verifiedOnRealLibrary.reportedCountNote: The first version logged the number of keys, which exceeds the number of items whenever one item has two spellings of its code, and printed '583 items, 626 titles recognised'. The count is of items now; see recognisedCount().

keysPerMatch.note: The bare key exists for DMM's maker prefix; a false match needs two makers to share a letter run and a number.

$comment: The optional Jellyfin / Emby integration. Read-only, off by default, and
inert until both `enabled` and an API key are set - a script that starts
talking to a server the user never mentioned is not one anybody should
install.
One request reads the whole library, cached for six hours, because the
alternative is a request per card and a listing holds 34 of them. A library
changes when the user adds a download, not while they browse.
The defaults are the products' own: 8096 is Jellyfin's port (Emby ships it
too) and the host is the documented localhost form. No real address belongs
in this file.
There is no single "play this" URL every version accepts. Jellyfin 10.9
moved the web client from hashbang routes (#!/video?id=) to plain hash
routes (#/video?id=), so the destination is a three-way setting rather than
a constant that is wrong on half the installs.
A work already held is skipped by bulk selection and upgraded by a hand
tick. Bulk means "everything she has", which is only worth having if it is
everything you lack; a hand tick is a deliberate request, and the only
reason to make one for a work you own is a fuller release.

protocol.authHeaderNote: Accepted by both Emby and Jellyfin. An API key comes from the server dashboard's API Keys page; no password is stored.
protocol.sizeAbsentMeans: held, size unknown - pickMagnet() then takes the largest release rather than comparing
protocol.sizeAbsentMeasured: On a real 10.10.7 server, no television episode carried MediaSources[].Size while every Movie did. A library whose items are Episodes can therefore be matched but never upgraded.
protocol.librariesNote: Used only to turn a library name into the ParentId the Items API wants. Needs an admin key; a non-admin key is answered with 403 and the sync then reads every library rather than failing.

measuredOnRealServer.note: The reason a library name is worth setting: the library holding the works this script is for was 582 items, against 15,288 for the whole server, and the largest single library held 9,890 that could never match. The library names themselves are the user's own inventory and are deliberately not recorded here.

$comment: The library is read in pages, and this is not an optimisation.
An earlier version asked for Limit=5000 and treated that as the whole
library. Against a real 15,288-item server it returned the first 5,000 and
stopped, so owned works beyond the cut were not recognised and would have
been downloaded a second time - the exact failure the integration exists to
prevent. A limit that is 'never reached in practice' is a claim to measure,
not to assume.
A short page is the only reliable end signal: TotalRecordCount and the page
size can disagree with what the server will actually hand over.
Sequential rather than parallel on purpose - it is someone's home server,
and four overlapping requests to save two seconds is not a trade worth making.
pagination.endSignal: a page shorter than pageSize, or all items collected

linkModeNotes.details: The work's page in the media server. The only link that can work - see whyNoDirectPlay.

$comment: The first version offered 'play directly' links as well: #/video?id=<id>
and the older hashbang #!/video?id=<id>. Both were wrong, and the way they
were wrong is worth recording so nobody adds them back.
Both load the video OSD, find that nothing is playing, and bounce to the
server's home page. Read from a real 10.10.7 install rather than guessed:
the component behind #/video registers a listener for an internal
SHOW_VIDEO_OSD event and reads NO url parameters at all, so the id is
ignored. The client only navigates there itself, once playback is already
under way. Its route table ends with a catch-all redirect to /home.html,
which is the bounce.
Nothing in the served bundles reads a query parameter on any route, and
PlayCommand appears only in the websocket remote-control handler. So there
is no URL that starts playback on this version, and the Jellyfin team says
the same on their own forum: 'I don't think this is currently possible.'
The item page has been at #/details?id= since before 10.9 and always
renders; playing is then one click, with resume, subtitles and transcoding
all behaving normally. A setting offering a broken alternative was removed
rather than kept: an option that always lands on the home page is worse than
no option, because it promises something the server cannot do.
whyNoDirectPlay.verifiedAgainst: Jellyfin 10.10.7, by reading its own served bundles
whyNoDirectPlay.upstreamPosition: not currently possible (jellyfin core team, forum)

$comment: The library is chosen from a dropdown filled by the server, not typed.
Typing was the first version and it was wrong: the name has to match
exactly, the user cannot see what the server calls its libraries, and a
near miss silently falls back to reading everything - which looks like the
setting being ignored. The list is one request to
/Library/VirtualFolders, made when the settings dialog is opened and when
Read library now is pressed.
The chosen value is always kept as an option even when the server does not
list it, so opening the dialog and saving cannot silently clear a working
setting just because the server was unreachable.
A disc centred on the cover, in the style of Jellyfin's own.
Its size and place are measured from the cover at runtime rather than
written in CSS, because the site gives the cover no width, height or aspect
ratio of its own - the carries only a src - so its box comes from
stylesheets that are not ours and moves with the viewport.
The diameter is chosen so the disc's AREA is about a ninth of the cover's,
which is what was asked for and is not a ninth of the width: on a 3:4 cover
that is about 43% of the width. A width-relative rule would look right on
one poster shape and wrong on the next.
A cover has no size until its image loads, so the first measurement is
usually 0x0; a ResizeObserver on each cover re-places the button when the
box becomes real and when the grid reflows.

ownedBehaviour.bulkSelection: skipped, and the count says so
ownedBehaviour.upgradePick: the smallest release at least 1.25x the held size, so one tier up rather than the biggest file on the page
ownedBehaviour.upgradeIgnoresWindowWhy: the window answers 'which release do I want'; an upgrade answers 'which is better than what I have', and a ceiling could exclude the only upgrade there is
ownedBehaviour.nothingLarger: nothing is sent, and the log says the work is already held

$comment: Order of preference, and why the largest wins inside the window.
See pickMagnet() in the userscript.
1.0 exposed two independent Min/Max boxes in MB. 1.1 replaced both with a
single Preferred size slider, because the pair could be set into an
inverted window and had to swap itself on save to recover. The bounds are
now derived from the one number:
min = preferredSize / SIZE_WINDOW_RATIO
max = preferredSize * SIZE_WINDOW_RATIO
Only preferredSize is persisted. The window is recomputed on load so the
two can never disagree. preferredSize defaults to 5GB, which yields a
512MB floor - the floor is the half that carries the intent, since its job
is skipping 200MB samples, so it is kept tight enough to keep doing that.
SIZE_LADDER is the set of stops the slider can take, in GB. Discrete stops
rather than a continuous range: every position is a round number a user
would type, the control stays keyboard- and screen-reader-navigable
without custom ARIA, and a stored preference is always one of a known set.
rule: clean magnets whose size is inside the window, and among those the one closest to preferredSize
if the window excludes every clean magnet, the largest clean one, flagged outside-window
if there are no clean magnets, a suspect one rather than nothing
when prefs.upgradeFrom is set - the work is already in the library - the smallest release at least UPGRADE_MIN_RATIO larger, or nothing at all

$comment: 1.1 and earlier took the LARGEST release inside the window. The window
is ten times either side of the preference, so that made the slider
almost inert: move it from 5GB to 20GB and both picked whatever the
biggest release happened to be. Every number the control displayed was
correct and none of them changed the outcome, which reads as a broken
control rather than as a wrong rule.
Now the preference decides, measured as the distance in log space so
that a 1GB and a 9GB release are equally far from a 5GB preference - the
question the slider asks is which release is about the size I asked
for, not which is furthest from it in absolute bytes.
The floor and ceiling are unchanged as hard filters: the floor still
skips 200MB samples and the ceiling still excludes absurd multi-hundred
-GB labels. Only the tie-break inside the window changed.
An exact tie goes to the larger release, keeping the old instinct that
between two equally-close releases the fuller one is the better answer.
When nothing fits the window at all the fallback is still the largest,
still flagged outside-window, so a preference never causes silence.
tieBreak.distance: absolute difference of natural logs, so the crossover between two sizes is their geometric mean
tieBreak.fallbackWhenNothingFits: the largest real release, flagged outside-window

$comment: Stock-install defaults for the products, shown as placeholders in the
settings form. These are publicly documented product defaults, not
credentials. Only what a user types is persisted.
aria2's port and RPC options come from its own manual; qBittorrent's from
its Web UI preferences and its /api/v2/app/version response.

aria2.auth: params[0] = 'token:<secret>' when a secret is set
aria2.note: No CORS headers, so GM_xmlhttpRequest is required.

qbittorrent.auth: SID cookie from the login response, sent back as Cookie

$comment: Measured against a live v5.2.3 WebUI, not assumed.
4.x sets SID. 5.x sets QBT_SID_<port> so several WebUIs can share one
host. A pattern anchored on SID alone matches nothing against 5.x,
because of the _8082 before the =, and the symptom is silence rather
than an error: no cookie, so every call silently falls back to the
userscript manager's own jar.
4.x answers 200 with the body Ok., or Fails. on bad credentials.
5.x answers 204 with an empty body, so the body alone cannot decide
whether a login succeeded and a Fails. check alone is dead code on a
current server.
The fix for the bug that made this client fail outright against a
stock install.
qBittorrent answers 401 to any request carrying a cross-site Origin or
Referer - which is exactly what a privileged request inherits from the
page the userscript runs on. Measured on a live v5.2.3:
login with Origin of the page's origin -> 401
authenticated GET with Referer of a foreign host -> 401
authenticated GET with neither -> 200
Its own documentation says to set both to the client's own base URL, so
every request in the userscript carries them. If the userscript manager
strips them anyway - Chrome forbids setting them and not every manager
passes them through - the failure stays a bare 401, and the only remedy
is one WebUI toggle. qbFailure() names that toggle instead of letting
a bare status code reach the log.
qBittorrent bans an IP after web_ui_max_auth_fail_count consecutive
failed logins (default 5) for web_ui_ban_duration seconds (default
3600). Without a cap, a batch of 17 magnets retrying a wrong password
would lock the user out of their own client for an hour - a
self-inflicted outage worse than the original bug. The limit is
deliberately under the vendor default so there is margin.
A CSRF-rejected login also returns 401 and may count toward that
total, which is why the fallback path matters.

note: Set-Cookie is a forbidden header name for a plain fetch and is not
surfaced by every userscript manager, so a missing cookie falls back to
relying on the manager's cookie jar rather than failing outright.
